$comment: What each platform pays for views (docs/CONTRACTS.md §21). The one place these numbers live: the web app imports this file; the API mirrors maxUsdPer1000 in settings.MAX_USD_PER_1000 (a pytest keeps them equal). All amounts are USD for every 1,000 views of a short vertical clip. Rates are estimates from public sources checked on asOf; the owner can set their real rate in Settings › Posting › Money. paysPerView is the default of 'Do I get paid here?'. It is true for YouTube, Facebook and X, so the owner sees what each clip probably earns there; the screens say that this only counts if the owner is in that app's paid program (kidRules). It is false for TikTok (Sweden is not eligible for Creator Rewards, and the clips are under 60 s) and for Instagram (the Reels bonus is invite-only); an app that is off shows $0 with 'Turn this on in Settings › Money if {App} pays you.' Every amount is a best guess. kidRules and kidCounts are the plain words the app shows; eligibility, unit and notes are the full details for maintainers.

youtube.label: YouTube Shorts
youtube.unit: engaged views (Shorts Feed views counted toward the Creator Pool; RPM is after YouTube's cut)
youtube.eligibility: You must be in the YouTube Partner Program and have accepted the Shorts Monetization Module. Today that means 1,000 subscribers plus either 10M Shorts views in 90 days or 4,000 watch hours in 12 months. From Feb 1, 2027, new applicants need 1,000 subscribers plus either 20M Shorts views in 90 days or 8,000 watch hours. Also from Feb 1, 2027, every partner channel must have at least 10M qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days to earn any Shorts revenue that month. Existing partners must accept the updated terms by Jan 31, 2027. Shorts over 1 minute that contain claimed content are not monetized.
youtube.kidNote: YouTube shares ad money from the Shorts feed and gives you about 5 cents for every 1,000 views, but from February 2027 only big channels with lots of views get paid.
youtube.kidRules: Only channels in the YouTube Partner Program get Shorts money. From February 2027 a channel also needs about 10 million Shorts views every 3 months.
youtube.kidCounts: People who watched your Short in the Shorts feed. Replays do not count.
youtube.notes: Official: the creator keeps 45% of their share of the Creator Pool. YouTube publishes no RPM. Third-party estimates for 2026 run $0.01-0.08, middle band $0.03-0.07; gaming sits at the low end. Per-video estimate = views/1000 x 0.05. The owner's '$0.5 per 1,000' is about 10x too high for Shorts; that is closer to long-form RPM.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.unit: qualified views (Creator Rewards Program; videos at least 1 minute long)
tiktok.tooShortNote: TikTok only pays for videos 1 minute or longer.
tiktok.eligibility: The account must be a personal account and the owner 18 or older, based in one of about 8 markets: US, UK, Germany, France, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and Mexico. It needs 10,000 followers and 100,000 views in the last 30 days. Videos must be original and at least 1 minute long. Sweden is not eligible, so this owner earns $0 per view today.
tiktok.kidNote: TikTok only pays for videos 1 minute or longer, and only in some countries, so our short clips from Sweden earn nothing from views on TikTok right now.
tiktok.kidRules: TikTok pays accounts with 10,000 followers in only a few countries. Sweden is not one of them yet.
tiktok.kidCounts: Views of videos that are 1 minute or longer.
tiktok.notes: There is no official RPM. Most 2026 guides say $0.40-1.00 per 1k qualified views, up to $1.20 globally; $0.70 is a derived midpoint. Per-video: 0 if the clip is under 60 s or the creator is not in an eligible market; otherwise qualifiedViews/1000 x 0.70. Show the rate only as an 'if eligible' estimate.

instagram.label: Instagram (Reels)
instagram.unit: bonus plays/views (invite-only Reels bonus only; ordinary creators get $0 per view)
instagram.eligibility: Ordinary creators are not paid for views. Instagram describes bonuses as limited-time and invite-only. Reports say the Reels bonus needs about 5M views over 3 months and runs only in the US and South Korea, possibly Japan too. Sweden is not included, so this owner gets $0.
instagram.kidNote: Instagram usually pays nothing for views. A few invited creators in a few countries get a tiny bonus, about 2 cents for every 1,000 views.
instagram.kidRules: Instagram does not pay for views. Only a few invited creators get a small bonus.
instagram.kidCounts: Views on Reels, and only for the bonus.
instagram.notes: Default to $0 per video. Turning on 'Do I get paid here?' (for an Instagram bonus invite) applies about $0.02 per 1k (range $0.01-0.05). Instagram publishes no rate; the typical value comes from one creator's 2024 bonus payouts.

facebook.label: Facebook Reels
facebook.unit: qualified views (watched at least 5 seconds; content at least 10 seconds long)
facebook.tooShortNote: Facebook only pays for videos 10 seconds or longer.
facebook.eligibility: Content Monetization is invite-only. You can express interest in the Professional Dashboard, but that does not guarantee an invitation. You must be in an eligible country; Sweden is on Meta's list as of 2026-10-08. You must follow Meta's monetization policies and finish payout setup. Meta publishes no follower threshold.
facebook.kidNote: Facebook pays a tiny bit, often about 5 cents for every 1,000 people who watch your clip for at least 5 seconds, but only after Facebook invites you to join.
facebook.kidRules: Facebook pays only after it invites you to join. Sweden can join.
facebook.kidCounts: People who watched for at least 5 seconds. Replays do not count.
facebook.notes: Meta publishes no rate. The dashboard 'Earnings Rate' (approximate earnings per 1,000 qualified views) is the best per-account number; use it when available. Post-Bridge (2025-12-21): $0.02-0.20 per 1k for most creators, about $0.01 for international or recycled content, above $0.30 for US-heavy original content; its worked example of $62 on 1.1M plays is about $0.056 per 1k. Per-video estimate = qualifiedViews/1000 x 0.05.

x.label: X (Twitter)
x.unit: total impressions (times the post was seen; derived from about $1.05 to $1.47 per 1,000 verified/Premium impressions x an assumed 5 to 20% verified share)
x.eligibility: Original Content Rewards replaced Creator Revenue Sharing in Sept 2026. You need to be 18 or older, in a listed country, and have an active Premium, Premium+ or Premium Business subscription. You also need 500 verified followers and 500k Home Timeline impressions from verified users in the last 90 days, not counting replies. You must apply and pass a review. Payouts come every 2 weeks with a $30 minimum. Copied, minimally modified, aggregated, automated and cross-platform reposted content is excluded.
x.kidNote: X only pays you when people who pay for X see your video, so most views earn nothing.
x.kidRules: You need to pay for X, have 500 followers who pay for X too, and X must say yes. X does not pay for clips you also post on other apps.
x.kidCounts: Every time your post was seen on X.
x.notes: There is no official rate. Payout data comes from one creator (ClimbX): about $1.23 and $1.05 per 1k verified impressions. Total-view figures assume a 5%, 10% or 20% Premium share. Formula: impressions/1000 x $0.12 (the X impressions count; video views when impressions are missing) when the verified share is unknown. Whether Sweden is a listed country was not checked. OCR excludes cross-platform reposts, so the real figure may be $0.
